label: heart100-s1
summary: This heart-disease model (training AUC 0.951) is mostly a linear score: removing its direct input-to-output edges drops training AUC to 0.720. Through those edges the model gives men, asymptomatic chest pain, a flat ST slope, more coloured vessels, higher cholesterol and blood pressure a higher predicted risk, and a normal resting ECG or normal thallium scan a lower one; a fixed thallium defect also lowers the score, a reading that rests on 15 training patients. Two hidden parts correct it. A gate, open on 86 training rows (85 of them with a normal resting ECG and 77 with no coloured vessels), adds back risk for those patients when the peak heart rate is low or ST depression is marked: for the typical patient, risk falls from 80% at 100 beats per minute to 7% at 200 beats per minute. A vessel-count part adds a second rising ca term, but a brake fitted to 17 rows cuts it for patients with many vessels for their age, so for the typical man aged 56 years the predicted risk is 94% with two vessels and 48% with three; this non-monotone step runs against the training outcomes of those rows (outcome rate 82%) and is the main caveat. A near-constant unit adds a small non-anginal chest-pain term. Exercise-induced angina and fasting blood sugar change 0 of 242 training predictions.
